title: fix(cli,lint): gate the i18n flow coverage bucket on the liveness ledger
body:
Fixes #11624

## The collision, reproduced before it was fixed

`os lint` computes i18n coverage and runs the authoring-rule registry in a **single pass over the same stack** — `Lint.run` calls `lintConfig` (→ `runAuthoringRules('lint')`, which carries `lintLivenessProperties`) and `computeI18nCoverage` one after the other. For the `flows` translation group the two halves pointed opposite ways. Measured on one stack, one run, at `cdbd9204b`:

| the author does | `i18n/missing-flow` | `liveness-planned-property` |
|---|---|---|
| **omits** `flows.*` from the bundle | **4** | 0 |
| **adds** it (`os i18n extract` scaffolds it) | 0 | **2** (one per locale bundle) |

The warn side's exact text: ``sets `flows` but this translation property is planned — declared, and a consumer is being built against it (not read YET).``

**On the "no third option" claim** — the card's central assertion, verified and *refined rather than falsified*. `os lint` has no per-rule or per-bucket suppression: the flags are `--skip-i18n`, `--include-platform`, `--i18n-strict`, `--default-locale`, and nothing else; the authoring-rule registry has no opt-out field. So a third option exists only in the coarse sense — `--skip-i18n` silences the **entire** `i18n/missing-*` family, i.e. exactly the signal #11485 was filed to restore. At the granularity of the `flows.*` keys themselves the card is right: there is no move that satisfies both rules. Under `--i18n-strict` the demand side becomes an **error**, so a project could be forced to author keys it is then warned for.

**The warn side is live, not inert** — confirmed. `lintLivenessProperties` walks locale-keyed bundles (`packages/lint/src/lint-liveness-properties.ts:391`, `asArray(stack.translations)` then one level into each locale), which is #11288's fix, and it fired on both locales of a real authored bundle in the measurement above.

⛔ **The warning is true and is not softened here.** No shipped screen-flow runner reads the group, so a translated wizard string is stored and never shown — the failure mode `validationMessages` was removed in 17.0.0 for. Its rule id is `liveness-planned-property`, i.e. *keep the key*, not *remove it*. The premature half is the demand, and that is what this PR gates.

## The fix

`collectExpectedEntries` in `packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-extract.ts` — the file's own docstring calls it "the **single** definition of what is translatable at all", consumed by both the coverage gate and the `os i18n extract` skeleton — now drops any entry whose top-level translation group the liveness ledger warns authors for authoring.

It gets that set from a new `authorWarnedProperties(type)` exported by `@objectstack/lint`, which returns **the very warn map `lintLivenessProperties` iterates**. That is the load-bearing choice: a demand side and a warn side can only be kept from contradicting each other by reading one verdict, and the first thing a second reader of the same JSON would do is drift from it.

Three properties follow from reading the ledger instead of switching on `flows` by name:

- **It self-activates.** The day an objectui screen-flow runner lands and the row flips to `live` (dropping its `authorWarn`, which exists precisely because nothing reads the group), both the coverage report and the extract skeleton pick the group up again. No flag, no follow-up edit.
- **It answers the card's ⚠️ sweep generally.** Any *future* group that acquires a warn is covered on the day it is marked, rather than re-opening this collision one group at a time.
- **Both halves fail quiet together.** An unresolvable ledger yields the empty set, which is also the state in which `lintLivenessProperties` warns on nothing. The state that must never arise is one of them speaking alone.

**Gating `os i18n extract` too is deliberate, not incidental.** The card names extract as the other door into the same trap ("adds it, e.g. from `os i18n extract`"), and `i18n-coverage.ts` carries an explicit invariant — the walker is shared "so the gated surface and the scaffolded surface can never disagree". Gating only the coverage bucket would have satisfied the letter of the suggested shape while moving the collision from lint-vs-lint to extract-vs-lint, and broken that invariant on the way.

**Join depth.** The match is on the group (`path[0]`) and stops there, because that is the only depth at which the warn side can fire for file-authored bundles: `getNested` fans out over **arrays**, and a translation group is a record keyed by target name, so a warned child row (`flows.label`) would resolve `data.flows.label` — a path no real bundle has — and warn nobody. Matching deeper would suppress keys nothing warns about.

## Measurements the card asked for

**Every line number re-measured on `origin/main`; ⛔ not reconciled with the card's 2026-08-24 figures.**

| the card said | measured at `cdbd9204b` |
|---|---|
| `lint-liveness-properties.ts:387` — `asArray(stack.translations)` | **:391** (drifted +4) |
| `authoring-rules.ts:1081` — registration | **:1082** (`name:`), call at **:1090**; `commands: ALL`, `surfaces: CLI_ONLY`, `tier: 'advisory'`, severity `warning` — all as described |
| `packages/spec/liveness/translation.json:63` — the `flows` row | **:63**, exact; `status: planned`, `authorWarn: true`, children `label`/`screens` both `planned` **without** `authorWarn` |
| `i18n-extract.ts` — `walkScreenFlows` | defined **:963**, called **:889** |
| `i18n-coverage.ts` — `COVERAGE_SOURCE` / `flow` bucket | **:192** / **:216** |

**The ⚠️ census — `flows` is the only affected group.** Of the 14 top-level groups in `translation.json`, 13 are `live`; `flows` alone is `planned` + `authorWarn`. The two other `authorWarn` rows in the whole `liveness/` tree are `field.json`'s `relatedListFilter` and `object.json`'s `externalSharingModel` — object/field *properties*, which the i18n walker never harvests into a translation bundle, so they cannot collide this way. Pinned as an **equality** (`toEqual(['flows'])`), not a `toContain`, so a second warned group goes red and is considered before it ships.

**Instrument discipline.** Every zero-hit reading here is paired with a positive control from the same instrument on a term independently known present and never a substring of the term under test — e.g. `flows` scores 0 in the committed example bundles while `objects` scores 4 in the same file; `embed-objectql` scores 0 screen-flow files while scoring 2 on the control term. The committed test carries the same pairing: the `flows`-is-warned assertion supplies the positive, and the six live groups supply the negatives.

## Tests

**Fixture triage of the existing #11485 pins, stated because "green" and "green by emptiness" are different things.** `i18n-flow-screen-coverage.test.ts`'s 13 pins are all about the bucket *itself* — which keys the walker harvests, how the report attributes them, what the skeleton looks like — and none of that changed. What changed is *when* it runs. Retiring them would have left the flip with no proof the bucket still works; leaving them to run gated would have turned four of them into assertions over an empty walk. So the file now mocks `authorWarnedProperties` to the empty set — the post-flip ledger — and keeps all 13 verbatim. The **gated** half is pinned next door in the new `i18n-flow-liveness-gate.test.ts`, against the **real shipped ledger**, so it goes red the day the row moves and someone must look at both halves together.

**Reverse verification — two ablations, each with its restore leg proven on disk.** Predicted direction first, both times "the gate test goes red, the as-if-live file does not":

- **A — remove the gate filter** from `collectExpectedEntries`: `i18n-flow-liveness-gate.test.ts` **5 failed / 16 passed**; `i18n-flow-screen-coverage.test.ts` stayed fully green, as predicted (it is as-if-live either way). The three gate pins that survived are the ones that do not route through the filter (the census, the negative control, the `warnedGroups: new Set()` self-activation pin).
- **B — remove the as-if-live mock** from `i18n-flow-screen-coverage.test.ts`: **9 failed / 4 passed**, proving those pins really do assert over a walked surface. The 4 survivors are the silent-either-way ones — and one of them, ``never emits the keys the schema refuses by name`` (`.toEqual([])`), is green-by-emptiness without the mock, which is exactly why the mock is there rather than the pins being retired.

Mutation was confirmed **on disk** each time by counting the removed text and the injected marker separately (`before=1 / after=0 / marker=1`) plus a `git hash-object` differing from the `HEAD` blob — never by an editor's exit code. Each script installed a `trap` on `EXIT INT TERM` calling a named restore function, which seeds `REPO_ROOT` from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and restores the **absolute** path `"$REPO_ROOT/$REL"` with `git checkout HEAD -- "$REPO_ROOT/$REL"` — pinned to `HEAD`, never the bare two-argument form, which restores *from the index* and would have put the mutation straight back on disk at exit 0. Restoration was proven by `git diff HEAD` being empty and the blob hash returning to the `HEAD` value, not by the trap having run. No rebuild was needed for either leg: both suites import the CLI's TypeScript **source** (`../src/utils/i18n-extract.js`), so no `dist/` sits between the mutation and the reading.

**Suites and gates, all at the final commit `52991eb9e`** (re-run after the `origin/main` merge, not carried over from the pre-merge tree):

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli test` — 184 files / **2102 passed**, after one unrelated flake was isolated (see below)
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test` — 81 files / **2298 passed**
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck` — clean
- `pnpm check:type-check-debt` — ``--re-measure: OK — 32 ledger entr(ies) re-measured in 214.8s, 1843 raw tsc error(s) total, none above its recorded number``, with ``surplus: none — every entry sits exactly at its measurement, so any new error is red``. **This is what typechecks the new test files**: both packages hide their tests from their own `tsc` program (`packages/lint/tsconfig.json` excludes `**/*.test.ts`; `packages/cli/tsconfig.json` includes only `src`), so the package `typecheck` scripts say nothing about them — stated rather than left to read as coverage they do not have.
- `pnpm check:i18n` — ``OK (9 package(s) — all bundles in sync, no undeclared authoring keys)``
- `pnpm check:i18n-coverage` — ``OK (12 config(s), 602 baselined untranslated string(s), none new)`` (see the ratchet below)
- Also green: `check:nul-bytes`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:where-matcher`, `check:query-options-erasure`, `check:type-check-coverage`, `check:cli-test-child-env`, `check:published-files`, `check:page-declaration-shape`, `check:slot-lookup`, `check:type-source-resolution`, `check:cli-command-ids`, `check:entry-guard`, `check:parse-guard`, `check:pnpm-filter-targets`, `check:agent-test-spelling`, `check:bash32-floor`, `check:react-page-adapter-contract`, `check:role-word`, `check:published-readme-links`, `check:doc-anchors`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:docs-single-h1`, `check:docs-redirects`, `check:docs-audit-scope`, `check:objectui-changeset`, `check:changeset-gate-self-tests`, spec's `check:docs` / `check:liveness` / `check:strictness-ledger` / `check:empty-state` / `check:variant-docs` / `check:skill-examples`, lint's `check:doc-formula-expressions` / `check:doc-security-posture`, and the script-form `check-doc-frontmatter`, `check-doc-route-spelling`, `check-docs-section-name`, `check-section-landing-index`, `check-empty-changeset`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-adr-0087-registration`, `check-ci-filter-parity`, `check-plugin-teardown-shape`, `check-comment-mask-adoption`, `docs-audit/check-affected-docs`, `docs-audit/check-drift-comment`, `pm/release-rehearsal-clone --self-test`.

**`pnpm lint` was narrowed, and the narrowing is measured rather than asserted.** ① The examined population is read from ESLint's own config, not guessed: run over all 9 changed paths, ESLint itself reports `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx`, `scripts/i18n-coverage-baseline.json` and the changeset `.md` as *"File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied"* — outside the linted population by config. ② The count comes from `--format json`: 5 in-scope `.ts` files, **0 errors, 0 findings**. ③ Invariance for untouched files: `eslint.config.mjs` is the repo's single config and never enables type-aware linting for **any** file — no `parserOptions.project`, no typed `@typescript-eslint` rules, a claim the config itself records as positive-control-measured at line 328. Each file's verdict is therefore a pure function of that file plus the shared config, and this diff touches no config, so it cannot move the verdict of a file it does not contain. CI runs the full farm regardless.

**One unrelated flake, isolated and filed, not swept.** The first full CLI run came back 1 failed / 2101 passed on `test/serve-node-env-production-default.e2e.test.ts` with ``✗ Port 49402 is already in use`` — a port bind race with a parallel agent in this shared container, not an assertion failure and nothing this diff can reach. Re-run in isolation: **3 passed**. The mechanism (a blind `Math.random()` port draw with no bind probe, under a docblock claiming it "never contends") is filed as #12441, unassigned, and ⛔ not fixed here.

## The i18n coverage ratchet moved down, and only where it should

`check:i18n-coverage` counts untranslated declared strings per example config against a shrink-only baseline. Removing the `flows.*` demands improved it on **exactly the three example apps that declare a `type: 'screen'` flow**, and on no other config:

```
examples/app-crm        93 -> 89
examples/app-showcase  424 -> 393
examples/app-todo      140 -> 120
```

The other 9 baselined configs are byte-unchanged — `examples/embed-objectql` and the 8 platform/plugin extract configs declare no screen flow, censused with the paired positive control described above. Regenerated with `node scripts/check-i18n-coverage.mjs --update`, the repair the gate itself prescribes for a ratchet DOWN, and confirmed independently: `os lint --json` on `app-crm` after the change reports `i18n/missing-flow: 0` while every other bucket is intact (`missing-object` 8, `missing-option` 34, `missing-field` 22, `missing-action` 2, `missing-navigation` 6, `missing-dashboard` 2, `missing-widget` 12, `missing-page` 3) — total 89 warnings, matching the new baseline exactly.

⚠️ `scripts/i18n-coverage-baseline.json` is a shared hot file; a sibling agent was observed running `check:i18n-coverage` in the same container during this work. If it conflicts at merge, the resolution is to re-run `--update`, never to hand-merge the numbers.

## Scope, and the two boundaries declared rather than crossed

**`packages/spec` is untouched** (ruling ②). The `flows` row keeps `status: planned` and `authorWarn: true`; the ledger is read, never written. ⛔ No row was flipped, reshaped, or dropped.

**`authorWarn` was not dropped from the row** (ruling ①). The warning is true and stays.

**Clause-② holds as determined at claim time.** The declared accept set is unchanged: no schema, no key, no validity boundary moves. `TranslationDataSchema` still accepts exactly the same `flows.*` keys it accepted before — an author who writes them still parses clean, and still gets the (true) liveness warning. What changed is which keys a *reporting* tool asks for. This is `declared = enforced` restoration on the tooling side.

**File-surface delta, stated because it exceeds the claim comment's literal list by one file.** The claim comment (5419223296) named `i18n-extract.ts`, `lint-liveness-properties.ts`, `authoring-rules.ts`, their sibling tests, and `translations.mdx`. Two departures, both upward-visible:

- **`packages/lint/src/index.ts` — one added re-export line.** `@objectstack/lint` publishes exactly two subpaths (`.` and `./runtime`), so a symbol added to `lint-liveness-properties.ts` (which *is* in the surface) is unreachable without its barrel line. The only alternative was to re-derive the ledger predicate inside `packages/cli` — precisely the drift this card exists to close. No API-surface artifact exists for this package, so the delta is the one line.
- **`scripts/i18n-coverage-baseline.json`** — a generated ratchet artifact this change necessarily moves, regenerated by the command the gate's own failure text prescribes.

And one file the retriage ruling named that turned out **not** to need editing: `packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-coverage.ts`. The ruling (5415947100) placed the remedy on `COVERAGE_SOURCE`; measurement showed the shared walker is the single definition, so gating there gives the coverage gate and the extract skeleton one consistent answer with **zero** edits to that file. Worth flagging because the claim comment's file surface omitted it while the ruling named it — the discrepancy is real, and it resolved in the direction of a smaller diff.

`packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts` was read (to confirm `commands: ALL` / `surfaces: CLI_ONLY`) and not edited.

## Docs

`content/docs/ui/translations.mdx` "Current boundaries" told an author the group is declared-not-applied and that the compile lint warns — but not what the tooling would do. It now carries the other half: `os lint` does not report `flows.*` as missing and `os i18n extract` does not scaffold them, both reading the same `planned` row; authoring the copy anyway yields the liveness warning and nothing else, which is telling the truth rather than asking for a deletion; and the day the row flips, both surfaces pick the group up with no flag to turn on.
